name: The Beekman
positioning: The Beekman, a Thompson Hotel: a restored 1881 building in Lower Manhattan built around a nine-story atrium, with restaurants by Tom Colicchio and Daniel Boulud
best_for: Travelers who want a historic building as their Lower Manhattan base
Guests who plan to dine and drink at the hotel's restaurants and bars

facts.text: The Beekman is at 123 Nassau Street in Lower Manhattan.
The nearest subway station is Fulton Street, served by the 2, 3, 4, 5, A, C, J and Z trains.
The building, once known as Temple Court, was first constructed in 1881.
The hotel opened in 2016 following a major restoration.
The interiors are by designer Martin Brudnizki.
The artwork in the rooms and suites was curated by Katherine Gass.
Rooms have aged oak floors and Carrara marble bathrooms with oversized rain showers.
Bathrooms stock D.S. & Durga amenities from Brooklyn.
At Temple Court, chef Tom Colicchio serves a menu of classics, old and new, reimagined.
Le Gratin is Daniel Boulud's Bouchon Lyonnais, inspired by his hometown of Lyon.
The fitness center is on two levels and has Peloton spin bikes.
A house car offers guests drop-off rides within a one-mile radius.

highlights.text: The hotel is built around a nine-story atrium.
The atrium was designated an interior landmark by the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission in June 2024.
The Bar Room sits beneath the pyramidal atrium skylight and serves an all-day menu by Tom Colicchio.
The Turret Penthouse is a duplex in the building's turret with a private terrace, 40-foot ceilings and a stone fireplace.
Laissez Faire is a cocktail lounge on the hotel's cellar level, with jazz musicians on Wednesday nights.

considerations.text: There is no spa on site.
A daily destination fee applies to each room.
Rooms are not perfectly soundproofed from guests on the floor.
